title: 2025-04-10 NovaRetail - Model selection & deployment options
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for a retail personalization product. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, desired context length (32k vs 8k), multilingual coverage (EN, ES, FR, PT), tool-calling for inventory/pricing APIs, latency/cost tradeoffs, and compliance requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS, EU data residency). Agreed next steps: share pricing SKUs, security pack, and schedule a technical deep dive + POC scope doc.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate you taking the time. I'll hand over to Priya to do a short agenda and then we'll dig into your use cases.
[00:12] Priya: Hi Samir, Elena, Tom, Jasmine, yeah we're excited to learn about NovaRetail's personalization roadmap. Quick agenda: 1) current arch + constraints, 2) model selection needs (open models), 3) deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), 4) next steps.
[00:28] Samir: Thanks. Quick context, we power personalized product recommendations and in-cart messaging across web and mobile. We need low latency for on-page render, usually 150-300ms for the model call, and we do multi-turn prompts sometimes for session-level personalization.
[00:45] Tom: Also multilingual, english and spanish primarily, latin america expansion so portuguese and french maybe. We need high fidelity for brand tone and to call internal pricing/inventory APIs, so tool-calling support is big.
[01:05] Priya: Gotcha. Are you currently running models in-house?
[01:10] Elena: We have a mix — smaller classification models on infra, but larger generation we've been using a third-party hosted API. Cost is creeping up and latency is variable when traffic spikes. We are evaluating whether to move to a dedicated pool or use a private deployment for EU data residency.
[01:28] Jasmine: From security side we need SOC2 (we have that already), SSO/SAML for access, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. Also need to verify EU region hosting or on-prem option for a subset of data.
[01:42] Priya: Makes sense — those are common. On model selection: are you leaning toward an open model family or proprietary models? Any requirements for function/tool calling like in-chat API calls to hit inventory?
[01:55] Samir: We prefer open models for cost predictability and ability to fine-tune. We care about long context — some product sessions can be 20k tokens when you include browsing history and chat. So the 8k limit is a blocker for some of our flows. We're evaluating models that support 32k.
[02:12] Alex: We commonly recommend a 2-tier approach: hosted for initial experiments and non-sensitive traffic, and Dedicated or Private for high-volume or regulated flows. Hosted supports our curated open models with verified perf profiles; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[02:35] Priya: For long context, there are a few open families that have 32k variants; we also offer kernel selection and compilation strategies to optimize for those sequences. There's also KV/prefix caching to avoid re-sending repeated context for session prompts which helps reduce tokens and cost.
[02:55] Elena: About KV cache, is that automatic or manual? We have a session store in Redis today.
[03:03] Priya: We can integrate with existing session stores; Redwood's runtime supports automatic prefix and KV cache population and retrieval, but you can also expose explicit cache hooks. It's configurable so you can control TTLs.
[03:18] Tom: On multilingual quality — if we want the same model to serve EN/ES/PT/FR, do you recommend a single multi-lingual model or language-specific models?
[03:29] Priya: Depends on latency/accuracy tradeoffs. Some open models are multilingual and do fine across languages, but they may be larger and costlier. Another pattern is language routing: route to smaller language-specialized variants in Dedicated to reduce cost. We can show benchmark numbers for Spanish/Portuguese.
[03:46] Samir: Can Redwood do function-calling for our inventory/pricing microservices? We need guaranteed structured outputs.
[03:53] Alex: Yes, hosted supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. For Dedicated/Private you get more control over network egress and can run the tool-caller inside your VPC for tighter security. There are policies for safe fallback if the tool-call fails.
[04:10] Jasmine: For Private we'd need HSM/KMS integration. Any customers running with BYOK?
[04:16] Miguel: We do support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations for Private deployments. Many enterprise customers use our KMS connectors and we can scope an audit of key rotation.
[04:27] Priya: Quick note on latency — 150ms P99 at production scale is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernels, but it depends on prompt shape and batching. Hosted can hit low latencies but less predictable under bursts.
[04:44] Elena: What's the impact of batching on perceived latency? We do single-request low-latency calls a lot for on-page personalization.
[04:52] Priya: There's a tradeoff. Continuous batching and dynamic dispatch often maintain low medians while improving throughput, but for strict P99 you may choose reserved capacity with smaller batch windows. We can configure per-route SLOs.
[05:07] Tom: On cost — do you have typical per-1M token costs for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:11] Alex: We'll share current SKUs in the follow-up, but generally Dedicated reduces per-token cost via reserved GPU hours and quantization options. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles to lower cost with minimal quality loss.
[05:26] Samir: About quantization — do you do post-training quant or compile-time kernels? We care about generation quality for product copy.
[05:34] Priya: We use quantization-aware kernels and recommend model-specific quant profiles. For high-fidelity copy we tend to avoid the most aggressive 4-bit profiles unless benchmarked on your eval set. We can run evals on a prompt set you provide.
[05:50] Jasmine: Regarding compliance, can we get SOC2 evidence and a data processing addendum? Also retention and deletion for customer PII?
[05:59] Alex: Yes, we'll share our security pack and DPA. For retention you can configure logs/audit retention. Private gives you the strongest guarantees because logs can be stored in your VPC.
[06:12] Samir: For POC, we'd like to benchmark two open models: a 32k multilingual variant and a smaller 8k multilingual variant, measure latency and quality on our retail prompt set, and test function-calling to our inventory API. Can Redwood run an on-prem or Dedicated benchmark?
[06:28] Miguel: We can run a Dedicated benchmark in a reserved pool or for Private we can run a scoped on-prem POC. Typical flow is: we run perf benchmarks on your prompts, we produce cost estimates and config suggestions.
[06:40] Tom: Timeline — we want to pilot in the next 6 weeks and make a decision by end of Q2. Is that realistic?
[06:48] Alex: Yes, that's reasonable. A hosted pilot can start immediately; Dedicated POC can be arranged in 2-3 weeks for infra provisioning. Private on-prem takes longer.
[07:00] Priya: Questions from Redwood: what are your average session lengths in tokens? And peak qps for personalization calls?
[07:07] Samir: Average session prompt is ~4k tokens, but heavy sessions can reach 18-22k when we include browsing history and multi-turn. Peak QPS for personalization endpoint is around 120 rps, but traffic is spiky during promotions up to 350 rps.
[07:26] Priya: Thanks. That helps sizing. For 32k models at 350 rps you'd want a Dedicated pool with autoscaling and burst capacity. We can model cost.
[07:36] Elena: Any concerns about model hallucinations calling inventory APIs? We need strict checks to avoid bad pricing messages.
[07:44] Priya: You can enforce tool-calls and post-call validation. We can also support guarded prompts + structured output parsing to ensure schema conformance. For critical messages we recommend a verification step before customer-facing outputs.
[07:58] Samir: On fine-tuning, we might want to tune for brand voice. Is that supported for open models on Dedicated/Private?
[08:06] Alex: Yes, we support fine-tuning and instruction tuning workflows for many open families. For Private we can run tuning inside your environment. We also recommend eval harnesses to measure regression.
[08:16] Tom: Any concerns about vendor lock-in if we do Private?
[08:20] Miguel: Private is customer-managed control plane but uses our runtime; configurations are portable and you can pin model versions. We emphasize standard model artifacts and provide export hooks for weights/avx where allowed by license.
[08:35] Jasmine: Can you confirm data residency options for EU? We need data never to leave EU for certain flows.
[08:40] Alex: Yes — we can host workloads in EU regions for Hosted/Dedicated, and with Private you can keep everything on-prem. We'll include region-specific notes in the security pack.
[08:52] [10:00] -- mid-call logistics, quick break, resumed --
[10:05] Priya: To make this concrete, we'll propose a POC plan: 1) Redwood runs benchmarks on two candidate open models (32k and 8k), 2) test function-calling against a staging inventory API (you provide endpoint + creds), 3) evaluate multilingual outputs against your eval set, 4) provide config recommendations and cost estimate.
[10:25] Samir: Sounds good. About the staging API: we prefer to host the staging endpoint in our VPC and Redwood's Dedicated pool can egress to it securely?
[10:35] Miguel: Yes, Dedicated can be set with secure egress policies; for Hosted we recommend a proxy in your VPC. For Private it can be internal-only.
[10:45] Tom: Are there any open model families you typically recommend for retail multilingual + long context?
[10:52] Priya: A few families we often evaluate: LlamaX-style large context variants, Mistral-derivative 32k variants, and some of the LLAMA-3 derivatives that have extended context. We'll include specific model IDs and perf profiles in the follow-up.
[11:10] Samir: Any regulatory issues with some open licenses? We need clarity on redistribution/derivative obligations if we fine-tune.
[11:18] Alex: We will surface license constraints per model in the model catalog and in the POC proposal so you can make informed choices.
[11:27] Jasmine: Action items for security review later — we will need contact points and a proposed timeline for SOC2 artifacts.
[11:33] Alex: We'll include a security contact and timing; typically sharing SOC2 metadata and DPA takes 3-5 business days.
[11:40] Priya: Any final questions?
[11:43] Samir: No, just please include concrete perf numbers and cost for the two models and routing options.
[11:49] Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll recap and send next steps.
[11:54] -- call end --
